quotes.text: We gathered all publicly available calculators from three widely-used medical platforms—MDCalc, Medscape, and QxMD—yielding 1,970 entries.

rationale: The source platforms are named, but no version or snapshot date is given and no route from a task to its source record is documented.

quotes.text: We gathered all publicly available calculators from three widely-used medical platforms—MDCalc, Medscape, and QxMD—yielding 1,970 entries.

rationale: The paper states data origin and collection from public calculator platforms. It does not document source licence or terms, consent, or IRB status for those sources.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README and docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 prompts/tool descriptions. The packet does not report representativeness of patient features against a named target population or descriptive population statistics.

quotes.text: The benchmark includes a safety test suite that measures unsafe outputs such as contraindicated medication orders, and a separate bias test

rationale: The paper reports both an unsafe-output test suite and a separate bias test. This satisfies both required components.

quotes.text: A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.

rationale: The packet reports developer-side controls, including a held-out split and canary strings, plus empirical leakage control statements in the same note. Although this evidence is in S4, it is part of the provided record for contradiction-capable evidence and directly addresses contamination controls.

quotes.text: the answer labels are stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox

rationale: The paper states that the agent cannot reach ground-truth answers at run time and names the mechanism: a separate evaluation service with no network path.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README and docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 prompts/tool descriptions. The benchmark depends on live Google Search and API models, and the packet does not report pinned data, software, simulator, judge model, or harness commit for a frozen evaluation environment.

quotes.text: we ran a scripted reference solution for each task through the grader; all 120 reference solutions were graded correct.

rationale: The paper reports scripted reference solutions run through the grader and gives the result. This fully satisfies the oracle solver criterion.

quotes.text: The grader checks both the intended state changes and that all other records remain unchanged

rationale: The packet reports state-changing write actions and says the grader checks both changed and unchanged records. Therefore NA does not apply.

quotes.text: A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks, and the chance success rate for each metric is reported

rationale: The paper reports empirical random-agent success and chance rates, showing trivial success is unlikely.

quotes.text: A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks

rationale: A do-nothing agent result is reported for all 120 tasks.

quotes.text: finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.

rationale: The benchmark reports validation of its grader on injected correct and incorrect outcomes with error figures.

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

contradiction_quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times
Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds; the temperature was set to 0.7

rationale: S1 reports temperature 0, a fixed seed, and three runs per task, satisfying the item. S4 contradicts the run count, seed policy, and temperature.

quotes.text: Model scores include 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Statistical testing of the two top-performing models employed paired permutation testing

rationale: The packet reports confidence intervals and a paired permutation test for top model comparison.

quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times

contradiction_quotes.text: All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times
Each task was run five times per model with independent random seeds; the temperature was set to 0.7

rationale: S1 reports the run count and seed/decoding policy. It does not state whether runs are independent, and S4 contradicts the run count and sampling policy.

quotes.text: where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead to account for clustering.

rationale: The paper reports 95% confidence intervals, bootstrapping over tasks, and patient-level resampling where tasks cluster by patient.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README and docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 prompts/tool descriptions. S1-S3 do not report action-sequence agreement, final-state agreement across reruns, or a pass^k all-runs metric.

quotes.text: Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 Team (2025) | Qwen3-235B-Instruct-2507

rationale: Some open models have dated/versioned identifiers, and S1 reports temperature and seed. The packet does not state a harness tag or commit matching the reported numbers.

quotes.text: the model issues an MCP tool call in JSON format with fields server , tool , and arguments

rationale: The paper specifies an MCP JSON action format and documents read/write side effects for some tools. Return semantics including errors are not documented on S1-S3 for every tool; S5 tool descriptions do expose read/write status for tools such as read-only SQL.

quotes.text: We ran conformance tests confirming that each tool behaves as documented.

rationale: The paper reports conformance tests and discloses simulated stubs. The packet does not show the simulation disclosure reaching S5, so the item is partial.

quotes.text: Writes are executed against a sandboxed copy of the record, and unnecessary or unsafe writes are penalised in the score.

rationale: The packet lists clinical write actions, states they are sandboxed, and says unsafe or unnecessary writes are penalised. It also states that the agent prompt tells agents writes are sandboxed.

quotes.text: The grader takes the final environment state as its input.

rationale: The paper names the grader input as final environment state and validates it on injected correct and incorrect outcomes with false-accept and false-reject rates. A rationale for non-state grading is not needed because the grader is state-based.

quotes.text: A private held-out split with hidden labels is kept off all public surfaces, and every released task carries a canary string.

rationale: The packet reports controls on answer leakage through tool and web access, a private held-out split, and canary strings on released tasks.

quotes.text: per patient subgroup by sex and race, and each table lists the number of cases in every slice.

rationale: The benchmark reports results per task family and per patient demographic subgroup, with case counts in each slice.

quotes.text: Task content was derived from clinical records of the kind found in hospital databases.

rationale: The paper states the broad source of patient records or seed state as clinical records. It does not report IRB/DUA/de-identification method or redistribution terms for environment data separate from the code licence.
